questions.q: The electric current through a wire varies with time as $I = {I}_{0} + \betat$, where ${I}_{0} = 20A$ and $\beta = 3As^{- 1}$. The amount of electric charge crossed through a section of the wire in $20s$ is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given that
Current $I = {I}_{0} + \betat$, ${I}_{0} = 20A$ and $\beta = 3As^{- 1}$

The instantaneous current is given by

$I = 20 + 3t . . . \left(1\right)$

Integrating equation (1), we have

\dfrac{dq}{dt} =$20 + 3t ⇒ {∫}_{0}^{q}dq = {∫}_{0}^{20} ( 20 + 3t ) dt ⇒ q = {∫}_{0}^{20}20dt + {∫}_{0}^{20}3tdt ⇒ q = {20t + \dfrac{3t^{2}}{2}}$_{0}^{20} = 1000C$

$

questions.q:
In a conductor, if the number of conduction electrons per unit volume is $8.5 \times {10}^{28}m^{- 3}$ and mean free time is $25fs$ (femto second), it’s approximate resistivity is: \left({m}_{e} = 9.1 \times {10}^{- 31}kg\right)$

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know $i = ne{Av}_{d}$
$⇒ i = \dfrac{V}{R} = \dfrac{VA}{ρl} = \dfrac{EA}{ρ}$
$ρ = \dfrac{EA}{i} = \dfrac{EA}{ne{Av}_{d}}$
Drift velocity can be written as ${v}_{d} = \dfrac{eE}{me}τ$
$ρ = \dfrac{EA{m}_{e}}{neAeEτ} = \dfrac{{m}_{e}}{ne^{2}τ}$
$= \dfrac{9.1 \times 1{0}^{- 31}}{8.5 \times 1{0}^{28} \times {\left(1.6 \times {10}^{- 19}\right)}^{2} \times 25 \times 1{0}^{- 15}}$
$\approx 1.65 \times 1{0}^{- 8}Ωm$

questions.q: The resistance of a conductor at $15 ° C$ is $16Ω$ and at $100 ° C$ is $20Ω .$ What will be the temperature coefficient of resistance of the conductor?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$16 = {R}_{0} \left[1 + \alpha \left($15 - {T}_{o}\right)\right]$

$20 = {R}_{0} \left[$1 + $\alpha\left($100 - {T}_{0}\right)\right]$

Assuming ${T}_{o} = 0 ° C$, as a general convention.

$⇒ $\dfrac{16}{20} = \dfrac{1 + \alpha \times 15}{1 + \alpha \times 100}

$⇒ $\alpha =$0 . 003{C ∘}^{- 1}$

questions.q: An aluminium wire is stretched to make its length, $0 . 4 %$ larger. The percentage change in resistance is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Volume of wire having cross-sectional area& $A$~and length~$l$~is,~$V = Al$

Resistance of a wire is given by,~$R = \dfrac{ρl}{A} = \dfrac{ρl}{\dfrac{V}{l}} = \dfrac{ρl^{2}}{V}$

As change in length is small,

$\dfrac{∆ R}{R} \times 100 % = \dfrac{2 ∆ l}{l} \times 100 % = 2 \times 0 . 4 % = 0 . 8 %$

questions.q: The $H$ amount of thermal energy is developed by a resistor in $10s$ when a current of $4A$ is passed through it. If the current is increased to $16A$, the thermal energy developed by the resistor in $10s$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Heat energy developed in the resistor due to current is given by,& $H = i^{2}Rt$. Therefore~

$⇒ H ∝ i^{2}$~(for $t =$ constant)

Now required ratio,~$\dfrac{H}{H '} = \left(\dfrac{4}{16}\right)2$

$⇒ H^{'} = 16H$

questions.q: A circuit to verify Ohm's law uses ammeter and voltmeter in series or parallel connected corrected correctly to the resistor. In the circuit :
options: ammeter is always used in parallel and voltmeter is series
Both ammeter and voltmeter must be connected in parallel
ammeter is always connected in series and voltmeter in parallel
Both ammeter and voltmeter must be connected in series
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Since the potential difference is measured across the two ends of the component, the voltmeter must always be connected in parallel to the components. An ammeter is an instrument which is used to measure the amount of current flowing in the circuit or through any component. It also consists of two terminals. The current is measured at a point.& Therefore, the ammeter must be connected in series with the circuit components.Ohm’s law states that voltage (potential difference) across a resistance in a circuit is directly proportional to the current flowing through it.Therefore, in Ohm’s law voltmeter is connected in parallel to the resistor and ammeter is connected in series.

questions.q: In a metre-bridge when a resistance in the left gap is $2Ω$ and unknown resistance in the right gap, the balance length is found to be $40cm .$ On shunting the unknown resistance with $2Ω,$ the balance length changes by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In first circuit:

For balanced condition, we get $\dfrac{2}{40} = \dfrac{X}{60} ⇒ X = 3Ω$

In second case:

Net resistance of the right side due to shunting becomes, $X^{'} = \dfrac{2 \times 3}{2 + 3} = 1 . 2Ω$

Again for balanced condition,

$\dfrac{2}{ℓ} = \dfrac{1 . 2}{100 - ℓ}$

$⇒ 200 - 2ℓ = 1 . 2ℓ$

$⇒ ℓ = \dfrac{200}{3 . 2} = 62 . 5cm$

Clearly, balance length changes by $22 . 5cm$.

A current of $5A$ is passing through a non-linear magnesium wire of cross-section $0 . 04m^{2}$. At every point the direction of current density is at an angle of $60 °$ with the unit vector of area of cross-section.
The magnitude of electric field at every point of the conductor is: (resistivity of magnesium $ρ = 44 \times {10}^{- 8}Ωm$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$I = \overset{→}{J} \cdot \overset{→}{A} = JAcos ( \theta )$
$5 = J\left(\dfrac{4}{100}\right) \times \cos ( 60 )$
$J = 5 \times 50 = 250Am^{- 2}$
Now, $\overset{→}{E} = ρ \times \overset{→}{J}$
$= 44 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 250 = 11 \times {10}^{- 5}Vm^{- 1}$

questions.q: Two electric bulbs, rated at  \left(25W, 220V\right)$ and \left(100W, 220V\right),$ are connected in series across a $220\text{V}$ voltage source. If the $25W$ and $100W$ bulbs draw powers ${P}_{1}$ and ${P}_{2} respectively, then:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${R}_{1} = \dfrac{V2}{P} = \dfrac{220 \times 220}{25} = 44 \times 44$

${R}_{2} = \dfrac{220 \times 220}{100} = 22 \times 22$

As resistance are in series current through them will be same.

$\dfrac{P1}{P2} = \dfrac{i^{2}{R}_{1}}{i^{2}{R}_{2}} = \dfrac{44 \times 44}{22 \times 22} = \dfrac{4}{1}$

Therefore, among the given options, the option matching is~${P}_{1} = 16W, {P}_{2} = 4W$

questions.q: A galvanometer has a resistance of $50Ω$ and it allows maximum current of $5mA$. It can be converted into voltmeter to measure upto $100V$ by connecting in series a resistor of resistance.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If we connect a high resistance($R$) in series with the galvanometer, it can be successfully converted into a voltmeter. Therefore,

Voltage drop across voltmeter:

$V = {I}_{g} \left({R}_{g} +R\right) ⇒ 100 = {I}_{g} \left($50 + R\right)$

$⇒ R = $\dfrac{100}{5 \times {10}^{- 3}} -$50$

$= 19950Ω$

$

questions.q: The number density of free electrons in copper is nearly $8 \times {10}^{28}m^{- 3}$. A copper wire has its area of cross-section $= 2 \times {10}^{- 6}m^{2}$~and is carrying a current of $3 . 2A$. The drift speed of the electrons is _____\times {10}^{- 6}ms^{- 1}.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the current through any conductor is given by

$I = nAe{v}_{d} . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the given parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required drift velocity of the electrons.

$\begin{cases}3 . 2 & = & 8 \times {10}^{28} \times2 \times {10}^{- 6} \times1 . 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times {v}_{d}\\ & ⇒ & {v}_{d} = \dfrac{3 . 2}{16 \times 1 . 6 \times 1000}ms^{- 1} \\ & = & 125 \times {10}^{- 6}ms^{- 1}\end{cases}$

questions.q: In the following circuit, the battery has an emf of $2V$ and an internal resistance of $\dfrac{2}{3}Ω$. The power consumption in the entire circuit is ______ $W$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we can see, two resistances of $2Ω$ in the middle portion(in both left and right side) are in parallel, so their combined resistance will be $\dfrac{2 \times 2}{2 + 2} + \dfrac{2 \times 2}{2 + 2} = 2Ω$. Now this resistance along with the topmost & bottommost resistance are in parallel again, so total resistance of the circuit will be,

${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{4}{3}Ω$

$∴ P = \dfrac{V2}{Req} = \dfrac{4}{\dfrac{4}{3}} = 3W$

$\dfrac{R}{S} = \dfrac{70}{30}$

Given here,~$R = 5 . 6kΩ$.

The,~$\dfrac{S}{30} = \dfrac{5 . 6 \times {10}^{3}}{70}$
